# Photo frames

Furniture to lay **over** a match photograph. Nothing is cropped, matted or
resized — the photo keeps every pixel it was shot with, and the frame goes on
top of it.

The middle of every file is transparent. Only the hairline border, the two
marks, the names and a soft shading along the bottom are painted; everywhere
else the photograph shows through untouched.

Generated by `npm run build:frames`. Don't edit these by hand — `npm run build`
deletes this whole folder and rewrites it.

## Which file

Two forms of each shape. **Use the PNG unless you have a reason not to.**

- **`.png`** — 4096 pixels on the long edge. Works in every app, including
  phones. Bigger than any photograph a phone takes, so it is always scaled
  *down* onto your picture, which costs nothing visible.
- **`.svg`** — vector. Exactly sharp at any size at all, including print and
  billboards. Only for Illustrator, Inkscape, Photopea or Affinity; Canva and
  phone apps can't use it.

Then pick the shape that matches your photograph:

| Shape | Pixels | For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `corner-photo` | 4096 × 3072 | 4:3 — straight off a phone or camera |
| `corner-square` | 4096 × 4096 | 1:1 — Facebook, Instagram feed, WhatsApp |
| `corner-portrait` | 4096 × 5120 | 4:5 — Instagram feed, tallest it allows |
| `corner-story` | 2304 × 4096 | 9:16 — Instagram and WhatsApp stories |
| `corner-wide` | 4096 × 2304 | 16:9 — video stills, thumbnails |

If your photograph is none of these shapes, crop the **photograph** to the
nearest one first. Never crop the frame, and never stretch it to a shape it was
not made for.

## How to use one

1. Open your photograph in any app that can put one image on top of another.
2. Add the frame as a layer above it.
3. Drag its corners until it covers the photograph exactly — edge to edge, no
   margin showing, nothing hanging off. Hold Shift while dragging if the app
   offers it, so the proportions stay locked.
4. Export.

### Keeping the full resolution

This is the part that goes wrong, and it is never the frame's fault — it is the
app quietly shrinking your photograph.

**The rule: the canvas must be the size of your photograph, not the other way
round.** A 4032 × 3024 photo needs a 4032 × 3024 canvas. If you build a design
at 1080 × 1080 and drop a 4032px photo into it, the export is 1080px and three
quarters of the detail is gone for good.

- **Photopea** (free, browser, no account) — File → Open your photo. The canvas
  is already the photo's exact size. File → Open & Place the frame, stretch to
  the edges, then File → Export as → JPG at quality 90 or more.
- **Photoshop / GIMP / Affinity** — the same: open the photo first, place the
  frame onto it.
- **Canva** — riskiest. Create the design as **Custom size** in *pixels*, typed
  to match your photo exactly. Don't start from an Instagram Post preset. On the
  free plan, check the download is not capped below that size.
- **Phone** — the Canva app can do it, with the same custom-size caveat. PicsArt
  can, with "Add photo". Snapseed can't — it has no layers.

Also: export as **JPEG at high quality, or PNG**. Anything that re-saves a JPEG
repeatedly loses a little each time, so work from the original photo, not from a
copy that has already been through WhatsApp.

## Please don't

- Recolour it, add a shadow or an outline to it, or change its opacity.
- Move the marks, resize one of them on its own, or retype the names.
- Stretch it to a shape it was not made for.

Every one of those changes the association's mark, and all are avoidable: if a
shape or a language is missing, it is one line in
`templates/social/frames/corner/frame.json` and a rebuild.

## What is on it

Everything comes from `brand/entities.yml`, not from anything typed per match —
which is why nothing on the frame can be edited, and why the competition cannot
go out misspelled.

- **Top left** — the cup's own mark, in colour, no ground behind it.
- **Top right** — the association's roundel. Its mint disc is part of the
  drawing, not a plate.
- **Bottom left** — كأس عمدة التاكلالت, and the season under it.
- **Bottom right** — رابطة شباب التاكلالت, the association's endorsement line.

The Arabic is outlined to paths, not set as live text, so the files mean the
same thing on a machine with no Arabic fonts installed — including a print
shop's.

### One thing to watch

In colour, the cup's chalice is drawn in `mint.900`, which is nearly black. On a
very dark photograph it goes quiet and only the gold crown reads clearly. If
that turns out to matter on real match photos, the fix is a one-ink variant of
that corner — ask, and it becomes another file here.
